chapter_theme: Reviling the guru (குரு நிந்தை): those who wound the teacher who gave a single syllable of mantra are reborn as dogs and worms; troubling the devotees, the chaste and the knowers ruins life, wealth, land and even Indra's throne; and to leave the guru's knowledge for ritual is to drop a gem and carry a stone.
structure_note: 530 sets out the base and the attained; 531 to 534 name the penalties for hurting teachers and devotees; 535 the ruin of falsehood before the guru; 536 the folly of leaving the guru's knowledge.

530.reading: The base do not honour even those who have attained, and speak words that hurt those close to them; those who keep to the path of the learned are the ones who have attained, and who but they gain the true gain?
530.nuance: பெற்றிருந்தார் may mean 'those who have attained' (the realised) or 'those who bore them' (parents). The verse turns on the word: the base do not honour those who have it, and only those who follow the learned get it.

531.reading: Those who speak so as to wound the excellent teacher who taught one syllable and its meaning so that it was understood will be born as a dog in the town for an age and then die as worms in the earth.
531.nuance: ஓரெழுத்து (one letter) is usually taken as a mantra syllable, often Om, but may mean any teaching however small. The variant பாரிடைக் does not change the sense.

532.reading: Those who cause ruin that troubles the minds of a chaste wife, of devotees and of knowers of the tattvas will lose wealth and life within a year; this is truth, by the command of Sadananda.
532.nuance: சதாநந்தி may be the Lord as ever-blissful Nandi. The pairing of the chaste wife with devotees and jnanis puts them in one class of the inviolable.

533.reading: Those who did evil so that the great ascetics who taught the one-syllable mantra grieved in mind will be born as outcast dogs and come as outcastes in a hundred forms, and die on earth.
533.nuance: This repeats 531 with மந்திரம் stated. நூறுரு may mean a hundred births or a hundred bodily forms.

534.reading: If the hearts of the Lord's devotees are troubled, country, land and their glories are destroyed; Indra's throne and the thrones of great kings come to ruin, by the command of our Nandi.
534.nuance: வாசவன் is Indra. The threat moves up from land to king to the king of the gods.

535.reading: If falsehood enters the presence of the true guru of the true path, the good path declines and knowledge does not stay; forgetting the ancient way, the many paths are ruined and famine comes too.
535.nuance: சந்நிதி பொய்வரின் may mean lying before the guru, or the guru's presence proving false (a false guru). சன்மார்க்கம் is the path of knowledge in Saiva usage.

536.reading: Like the fate of one who lets fall the great gem he held and carries a stone stuck to his body, and like one who eats bitter things while ghee, milk and curd stand at hand: such is the ritualist beside the knower.
536.nuance: The last words கன்மிஞானிக்கு ஒப்பே are compressed: perhaps 'such is the karmi compared with the jnani', or 'such is one who leaves the jnani for the karmi'. The images make plain that something precious at hand is exchanged for something worthless.

links.note: Commentators read the Kural's வேந்தன் as Indra, who falls midway if those of exalted vows are angered; Tirumular names Indra's throne (வாசவன் பீடம்) and great kings' thrones as ruined when devotees are troubled.
Both start from not honouring the great (பேணாது, பேணார்); the Kural warns of ills that do not leave, Tirumular calls those who do it base.

Both use the good thing at hand left for a worse one: the ripe jackfruit for the wild date in 201, the gem for a stone and ghee and curd for bitter food in 536. One is about another man's wife, the other about leaving the guru's knowledge.

A near-repeat: 531 and 533 both threaten those who wound the teacher of the one syllable (ஓரெழுத்து) with birth as a dog (சுணங்கனாய்ப் பிறந்து) and death on earth (மாய்வர் மண்ணிலே). 533 makes the syllable a mantra (மந்திரம் ஓரெழுத்து) and adds a hundred outcaste births.

531 says those who speak to wound the teacher of the one syllable die as worms on the earth (மாய்வர் மண்ணிலே); Kural 898 says if the hill-like great are slighted, those who seemed to stand forever vanish from the earth with their line (மாய்வர் நிலத்து). The Tirumanthiram applies the Kural's warning about the great to the guru, with the same closing verb.

531 honours the teacher who made one syllable and its meaning understood (ஓரெழுத்து ஒருபொருள் உணரக் கூறிய); Thiruppugazh 176 calls Murugan the child guru (குழந்தைக் குருநாதா) who spoke the secret of the pranava into Siva's ear (செவியுட் பிரணவ ரகசியம்). The one-syllable teaching that makes a guru inviolable in 531 is, in the song, given by the son to the father.

532 says those who trouble the minds of a chaste wife, devotees and knowers lose wealth and life within a year (அத்தமும் ஆவியும் ஆண்டொன்றில் மாண்டிடும்); Kural 900 says even those with overwhelming support do not survive if those of great distinction are angered (உய்யார் ... சீரார் செறின்). Both make offence against the inviolable fatal whatever one's means; 532 widens the class to the chaste wife.

535 says falsehood before the true guru makes the good path decline and brings famine (பஞ்சமும் ஆமே); 519 says worship by a Brahmin who has only the name brings disease to kings and famine to the land (பஞ்சமும் ஆம்). In both a falsehood at the sacred centre is answered by famine on the land.

535 traces famine to falsehood in the presence of the true guru; Kural 559 traces failed rain to a king who bends justice (முறைகோடி மன்னவன் செய்யின் ... ஒல்லாது வானம் பெயல்). The same logic, a fault at the centre spoiling the land's harvest, runs in the guru's presence and in the king's rule.

536 likens the ritualist beside the knower to one who eats bitter things while ghee, milk and curd stand at hand (கைப்பட்ட நெய்பால் தயிர்நிற்க); Kural 100 likens harsh speech, when sweet words are there, to grabbing raw fruit while ripe fruit is at hand (கனியிருப்பக் காய்கவர்ந்தற்று). The same figure of choosing the worse food beside the better serves speech in the Kural and the path of knowledge in the Tirumanthiram.

source_issues: 531: variants பாரிடைக் for வாரிடைக் and படிகுவர், பழகுவர் (apparently for மாய்வர்).
532: variants மாய்ந்திடுஞ் for மாண்டிடும் and சொன்னோம்.
